prerequisites: Having studied Physics in 2nd year of Bachillerato (Spanish High School equivalent)
Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, basic geometry, trigonometry, and derivation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems within their area of study, mainly fostering the reasoning aspect over pure memorization.
Ability to plan and organize personal work.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability for effective oral and written communication.
Possess necessary learning skills to undertake further studies or improve their training with a certain degree of autonomy.
Have motivation for quality and continuous improvement and act rigorously in professional development.
Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of fields and waves and their application to solving problems typical of engineering.
Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of electromagnetism and their application to solving problems typical of engineering.
Understand the concept of a wave and know its mathematical characterization as well as basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Electrostatics: Electric charge, Coulomb's Law, Electrostatic field and potential created by point charges. Obtaining electrostatic field and potential created by charge distributions without total symmetry. Obtaining the electric field created by charge distributions with total symmetry: Gauss's Theorem. Obtaining the electrostatic potential created by these charge distributions. Conductors. Dielectrics: Capacitors.
Electric Current: Current intensity and density. Ohm's Law. Resistance: associations of resistances. Joule effect. Generators: Electromotive force. DC circuits.
Magnetostatics: actions of magnetic fields on currents: Magnetic field. Magnetic induction. Lorentz Law. Hall effect. Magnetic force on an electric current. Magnetic moment on a loop.
Magnetostatics: magnetic fields created by currents: Biot-Savart Law: application to conductors with symmetries of interest. Force between currents: redefinition of ampere. Ampere's Theorem.
Time-varying electromagnetic fields: Electromagnetic induction: Faraday-Henry Law. Self-induction and mutual induction.
Waves: Concept of a wave. Wave equation. Classification of waves. Harmonic waves. Sound waves. Standing waves in vibrating strings. Doppler effect.
Laboratory Practical 1: Electrical measurements with multimeters. Experimental verification of Ohm's law.
Laboratory Practical 2: Experimental verification of capacitor charging transient.
Laboratory Practical 3: Experimental verification of magnetic fields created by infinite and finite straight conductors and circular loops.
Laboratory Practical 4: Experimental verification of physical parameters associated with standing waves generated in vibrating strings.
teaching_methods: Presentation and defense of problems, assignments, projects
Use of measurement equipment in the laboratory
Use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing software
Individual and group study of theoretical-practical contents
Preparation of reports on proposed assignments
Use of virtual platforms for teaching activities

assessment_methods.method: Objective written theoretical and/or practical individual tests
Laboratory practice evaluation or final laboratory practice exam
Attendance, behavior, attitude control, and professor's notes on active participation in individual and collective activities

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum of 75% participation in all in-person activities is required. The final grade is calculated as: Final Grade = CT + CEF*(8.5-CT)/8.5 + CL, where CT (Theory Grade) is out of 4 points, CL (Laboratory Grade) is out of 1.5 points, and CEF (Final Exam Grade) is out of 8.5 points. To pass, a final grade of at least 5 points is needed, with a minimum of 3 points on the final exam (CEF) and 0.5 points in laboratory practices (CL). Failure to meet these minimums results in a maximum final grade of 4 points. For global assessment, the final grade is Final Grade = CEF + CL, requiring a minimum of 5 points overall and 0.5 points in CL. For extraordinary calls, continuous assessment students retain CT and CL (if passed) and retake CEF; global assessment students retake both CEF and CL.
